subject: architecture

source.qualification: NAAB Conditions for Accreditation, 2020 Edition (revised March 19, 2026) — Program and Student Criteria
source.track: US professional degree accreditation · eight Program Criteria (PC.1–PC.8) and six Student Criteria (SC.1–SC.6) every accredited architecture curriculum must demonstrate

note: Units follow the Conditions' criteria in source order: Program Criteria (PC.1–PC.8) then Student Criteria (SC.1–SC.6). PC.7 (Learning and Teaching Culture) is a program-culture criterion with no student content and is omitted. The understanding-level criteria anchor the foundational-to-advanced lessons; the ability-level synthesis criteria (SC.5–SC.6) carry the expert work.

program.title: PC.1 Career Paths
topics: Paths to becoming a licensed architect in the United States
The range of career opportunities using the discipline's skills and knowledge

program.title: PC.2 Design
topics: The role of the design process in shaping the built environment
Design processes integrating multiple factors, in different settings and scales of development, from buildings to cities

program.title: PC.3 Ecological Literacy and Responsibility
topics: The dynamic between built and natural environments
Mitigating climate change through ecological and advanced building performance principles
Adaptation and resilience

program.title: PC.4 History and Theory
topics: Histories and theories of architecture and urbanism
Local, national and global social, cultural, economic and political contexts

program.title: PC.5 Research and Innovation
topics: Engaging and participating in architectural research
Testing and evaluating innovations in the field

program.title: PC.6 Leadership and Collaboration
topics: Approaches to leadership in multidisciplinary teams
Stakeholder constituents and dynamic physical and social contexts
Effective collaboration skills for complex problems

program.title: PC.8 Cultural and Social Contexts
topics: The broad range of cultural and social contexts
Built environments that support and include people of different backgrounds, resources and abilities

program.title: SC.1 Health, Safety, and Welfare in the Built Environment
topics: The impact of the built environment on human health, safety and welfare
Multiple scales, from buildings to cities

program.title: SC.2 Professional Practice
topics: Professional ethics
Regulatory requirements
Fundamental business processes relevant to architecture practice

program.title: SC.3 Regulatory Context
topics: Fundamental principles of life safety
Land use and current laws and regulations applying to buildings and sites
The evaluative process architects use to comply with regulations

program.title: SC.4 Technical Knowledge
topics: Established and emerging systems, technologies and assemblies of building construction
Assessing technologies against design, economics and performance objectives

program.title: SC.5 Design Synthesis
topics: Design decisions synthesizing user requirements, regulatory requirements and site conditions
Accessible design
Measurable environmental impacts of design decisions

program.title: SC.6 Building Integration
topics: Building envelope systems and assemblies
Structural, environmental control and life safety systems
Measurable outcomes of building performance
